elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its Affiliates against third-party claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The added clause requires Vendor to “defend” Customer and its Affiliates against any third-party claim arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its Affiliates against third-party claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The added clause requires Vendor to “indemnify, and hold harmless” Customer and its Affiliates from the covered IP claims and resulting damages, costs, and expenses.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its Affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of Applicable Law.
elements.evidence: The defence obligation applies to any third-party claim arising from “Vendor's breach of Applicable Law.”

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its Affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of Applicable Law.
elements.evidence: The indemnification obligation applies to any third-party claim arising from “Vendor's breach of Applicable Law.”

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its Affiliates against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: The defence obligation covers third-party claims arising from unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, an operative formulation of a Vendor-caused data breach.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its Affiliates against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: The indemnification obligation covers third-party claims arising from unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its Affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: The defence obligation expressly covers third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its Affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: The indemnification obligation expressly covers third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its Affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: The defence obligation expressly covers third-party claims arising from Vendor's wilful misconduct.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its Affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: The indemnification obligation expressly covers third-party claims arising from Vendor's wilful misconduct.

elements.element: Customer must provide Vendor prompt notice of an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: The clause requires Customer to give Vendor “prompt written notice of the claim.”

elements.element: Vendor must control the defence of an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that “Vendor shall control the defence of the claim.”

elements.element: Customer must provide reasonable cooperation in the defence of an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly requires Customer to “provide reasonable cooperation.”

elements.element: Any Customer indemnity must be limited to third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content or Customer's breach of Applicable Law.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Customer's indemnity obligations, if any, are limited to third-party claims arising out of Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law, excluding other indemnity subjects.

elements.element: Vendor must provide an IP indemnity for third-party claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The added clause provides defence and indemnification for third-party IP claims concerning the Services or Deliverables.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims caused by Customer modifications to the Services or Deliverables.
elements.evidence: No Customer-modification exclusion appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims caused by combinations with items not supplied or approved by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims resulting from compliance with Customer-provided specifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-specifications exclusion appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: The IP infringement remedies must include procuring the right for Customer to continue using the affected Services or Deliverables.
elements.evidence: The rendered language contains no procurement-of-rights remedy. Section 9.3 references remedies in Section 20.5, but no such operative remedy is supplied here.

elements.element: The IP infringement remedies must include modifying the affected Services or Deliverables so they are non-infringing.
elements.evidence: No modification remedy is operative upon an IP claim. Section 19.4's repair or re-performance language applies only to breaches of Sections 19.1 or 19.2.

elements.element: The IP infringement remedies must include replacing the affected Services or Deliverables with non-infringing substitutes.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 mentions replacement only for breaches of Sections 19.1 or 19.2 and does not create a replacement remedy triggered by an IP claim.

elements.element: If procurement, modification, or replacement is unavailable, the IP infringement remedies must include a refund for the affected Services or Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4's refund is conditioned on failure to cure a breach of Sections 19.1 or 19.2; no refund is expressly triggered by inability to resolve an IP claim.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnification liability must be subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No three-times-annual-fees cap appears. Section 21.3 instead identifies indemnification obligations as “Excluded Claims,” with no stated super-cap.

result.reason: The operative insertion fully supplies the preferred Vendor defence and indemnity triggers, beneficiaries, procedures, and Customer-indemnity limitation without changing unrelated commercial terms. It does not satisfy the fallback because all three IP exclusions, the infringement-specific remedy package, and the 3× annual-fees super-cap are absent. The drafting quality is materially undermined by leaving the inserted indemnity clause unnumbered and failing to resolve the existing reference to remedies in Section 20.5.
